note: Entertainment & Media lesson, content v3 (14 words). Course level B1.1 (Gateway level 9); units Media (Criticize) and Magic (the rest).

words.meaning: To say what you think is bad or wrong about someone or something.
situations: Many newspapers criticized the government for raising taxes again.
gaps: The film was ______d by critics for its weak ending.
Please don't ______ my cooking if you won't help in the kitchen.
hints: The opposite of praising someone.
Starts with 'crit-' and ends with '-ize'.

words.meaning: Special abilities that cannot be explained by science or the laws of nature.
situations: In the story, the old woman uses her supernatural powers to see the future.
gaps: She claims she has ______ and can move objects with her mind.
Superheroes in comics often have ______, like flying or reading minds.
hints: Abilities beyond what is natural or scientific.
Two words: 'super-' + 'natural' + another word for strengths.

words.meaning: To drink blood from people's bodies, as vampires do in stories.
situations: In the legend, the vampire comes out at night to suck people's blood.
gaps: Vampires sleep in coffins by day and ______ at night.
Mosquitoes, like vampires, ______ — but only a little!
hints: What vampires do to their victims.
Starts with 'suck' and ends with 'blood'.

commonMistakes.why: The verb is 'suck' (pull in with the mouth), not 'sock'.

words.meaning: Magic that claims to talk to or control the dead.
situations: The villain in the novel practises necromancy to bring dead soldiers back to life.
gaps: The dark wizard was punished for practising ______ — raising the dead.
In fantasy games, ______ lets a character control skeletons and ghosts.
hints: The practice (not the person) of using magic with the dead.
Ends in '-mancy'.

commonMistakes.why: 'Necromancy' is the practice; the person is a 'necromancer'.

words.meaning: A person who claims to tell your future by looking at the lines on your hand.
situations: At the fair, a palm reader looked at my hand and said I would travel a lot.
gaps: The ______ studied the lines on my hand and said I'd live a long life.
She paid a ______ to look at her hand and tell her about her love life.
hints: Reads the lines on the inside of your hand.
Two words: a part of the hand + someone who reads.

commonMistakes.sentence: The palm reader read my coffee cup.
commonMistakes.correction: The coffee cup reader read my coffee cup.
commonMistakes.why: A palm reader reads hands, not cups.

words.meaning: A person who claims to tell your future from the shapes left by coffee at the bottom of a cup.
situations: After we drank our Turkish coffee, the coffee cup reader turned my cup over and told me my future.
gaps: My grandmother was a ______ — she looked at the coffee left in your cup and predicted your future.
After you finish your Turkish coffee, the ______ turns the cup upside down and reads the shapes.
hints: Reads the marks left after drinking a hot drink.
Three words: a drink + a container + someone who reads.

commonMistakes.sentence: She is a coffee cup reader of hands.
commonMistakes.why: A coffee cup reader reads cups; someone who reads hands is a palm reader.

words.meaning: To break a spell or undo its effects so things go back to how they were.
situations: Only a kiss from a prince could reverse the spell and turn the frog back into a man.
gaps: The witch is the only one who can ______ the curse she put on him.
They searched for a magic potion to ______ the spell.
hints: To undo a spell — also used for turning a car backwards.
Starts with 're-', means 'go back'.

commonMistakes.sentence: The wizard reversed back the spell.

words.meaning: A person who uses magic to talk to or control the dead.
situations: The necromancer raised an army of skeletons from the old graveyard.
gaps: The ______ called the spirits of the dead to answer his questions.
In the game, the ______ can bring dead enemies back to fight for him.
hints: The person (not the practice) who works magic with the dead.
Ends in '-er'.

commonMistakes.why: The practice is 'necromancy'; 'necromancer' is the person.

words.meaning: A woman who is believed to have magic powers, often shown with a black hat and a broom.
situations: The witch flew over the village on her broomstick and cast a spell on the king.
gaps: The old ______ mixed a potion in her big black pot.
For Halloween, she dressed up as a ______ with a pointed hat and a broom.
hints: A woman with magic powers who flies on a broomstick.
Sounds like 'which'.

commonMistakes.sentence: Which witch? The which with the black hat.
commonMistakes.correction: The witch with the black hat.
commonMistakes.why: 'Which' is a question word; a woman with magic is a 'witch'.

words.meaning: The twelve star signs, such as Leo or Pisces, that people link to the month they were born in.
situations: She was born in August, so her zodiac sign is Leo.
gaps: There are twelve ______, from Aries to Pisces.
Some people believe your ______ shows what kind of personality you have.
hints: Leo, Virgo, Scorpio and nine more.
Two words: starts with 'Z'.

commonMistakes.why: Ask about someone's 'zodiac sign' or 'star sign', not just 'zodiac'.

words.meaning: A short prediction about your future, based on your star sign and the position of the stars.
situations: My mum reads her horoscope in the newspaper every morning.
gaps: According to my ______, I'm going to meet someone special this week.
She checks her ______ online every day to see what the stars say.
hints: A daily or weekly prediction in magazines based on your star sign.
Starts with 'horo-'.

commonMistakes.sentence: I read my zodiac sign in the newspaper today.
commonMistakes.correction: I read my horoscope in the newspaper today.
commonMistakes.why: Your zodiac sign is Leo, Aries…; the prediction you read is your 'horoscope'.

words.meaning: A place where dead people are buried.
situations: Nobody wanted to walk through the cemetery at midnight because of the ghost stories.
gaps: My grandfather is buried in the ______ near the church.
The ghost story takes place in an old ______ full of broken gravestones.
hints: A large area with graves and tombstones.
Ends in '-tery', not '-tary'.

commonMistakes.why: The spelling is 'cemetery' — three e's, no 'a'.

words.meaning: A dream in which you know that you are dreaming and can sometimes control what happens.
situations: In my lucid dream I knew I was asleep, so I decided to fly over the city.
gaps: I had a ______ last night — I knew I was dreaming, so I chose to fly.
In a ______, you realise you are dreaming and can change the story.
hints: A dream where you are aware it isn't real.
The first word means 'clear'.

commonMistakes.sentence: I had a lucky dream where I knew I was dreaming.
commonMistakes.correction: I had a lucid dream where I knew I was dreaming.
commonMistakes.why: 'Lucid' means clear and aware; 'lucky' means fortunate.

words.meaning: The hair that grows on a man's chin and cheeks.
situations: The old wizard had a long white beard that reached down to his belt.
gaps: The wizard stroked his long grey ______ while he thought.
He stopped shaving and grew a thick ______.
hints: Hair on a man's face, like a wizard's long white one.
Sounds like 'beer' + 'd'.

commonMistakes.sentence: The wizard had a long white bread.
commonMistakes.correction: The wizard had a long white beard.
commonMistakes.why: 'Bread' is food; facial hair is a 'beard'.
